Replay

Coordinator-backed RTC signaling

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Explicit providers and P2P rosters

Rendezvous is a bounded JSON frontend alongside the native authority Service. It borrows that Service and a raw Websocket listener. Poll the listener once, route binary messages to auth.service_receive, route text to rendezvous_receive, and call rendezvous_pump every frame. Close the frontend before closing its borrowed owners.

A create/join request must name the exact room code derived from the current signed authority view. The frontend issues a fresh cryptographic challenge on that WebSocket connection. A response consumes the challenge once and must arrive before its deadline. auth.rendezvous_verify checks the member key, registered incarnation, live grant and requested role. Only the approved owner receives RTC peer ID 1. Other enabled members receive increasing IDs. A disconnected RTC instance may retain its ID through authenticated continuation; a fresh instance does not gain that reservation merely by presenting the member key. A second live connection for an already admitted identity is rejected.

The relay introduces an authority star and overwrites the sender ID itself. Only admitted peers can relay SDP/ICE, and clients can signal only the authority. It never carries gameplay packets. New authority terms remove old signaling memberships. Expired grants, disabled/rebound members, disconnected sockets and expired challenges are pruned. Existing direct data channels remain subject to Room's gameplay lease and epoch checks, independently of signaling.

Defaults allow 32 signaling connections, five-second challenges, a 15-second continuation grace period, a burst of 64 messages and 32 messages/second per connection. JSON is limited to 32 KiB and nesting depth 16. Outgoing backpressure disconnects the affected signaling peer instead of silently dropping an introduction or SDP message. The shared listener and control service retain their own packet/connection budgets.

Client setup uses a stable Rtc_Grant_Auth containing a verified View, identity and provisioned key:

Odin
cfg := transportgd.rtc_grant_config(&authorization, signaling_url, is_owner)
transportgd.rtc_open(&rtc, cfg)

The generic Rtc_Config.authorize callback can answer other compatible challenged providers. Its returned text is borrowed for the immediate send. Authenticated registration requires strict equality with the requested room; unauthenticated legacy relays remain supported by ordinary rtc_open calls.

Room owns this authorization state and copied provider configuration through host/client role changes. Its Migration_Transport names RTC explicitly, using the configured provider URL plus the room/content/epoch/owner-derived code. The coordinator's existing native endpoint record and wire formats are unchanged; RTC destinations are not interpreted as ENet addresses.

Authenticated registrations receive a random continuation token. On signaling loss the frontend holds the identity/peer ID for the bounded grace period. A reconnection must answer a fresh challenge and present that token; comparisons use constant-time verification. Disabled/rebound members, obsolete terms and expired reservations cannot resume. Tokens are invalidated with the room term. They supplement member authentication and do not replace it.

rtc_grant_config enables automatic signaling recovery. It retries after 500 ms, retains healthy peer connections and fragment state, and checks that the resumed ID/token match. Incomplete connections are deliberately rebuilt, with replacement introductions to both endpoints. A rejected or expired continuation surfaces an error for the enclosing session to handle; it never silently adopts a new ID. Legacy relays remain opt-in and need not implement continuation.

Real-browser gates cover host/client recovery with unchanged connection serials, packets received during the outage, wrong-token rejection and late join after recovery. Cavecrawl also continues in the same epoch with no migration. Its planned/crash and broader migration gates remain available. Public provisioning, TLS/TURN deployment and other browser engines still need acceptance. The local fixture contains test keys and is not a production account/admission service.

Explicit providers and P2P rosters#

rendezvous_provider_init accepts a borrowed Rendezvous_Provider with a clock, current scope, enabled-identity predicate and fixed-proof verifier. The provider owns credential persistence and policy. The common frontend still enforces the per-connection random challenge, one-time use, deadline, duplicate/reservation checks and packet budgets. Its verifier callback consumes the existing 116-byte proof slot and returns an exact identity and room code. rendezvous_init wraps the authority Service in this interface and preserves the existing lease policy.

Rendezvous_Config.mesh allows introductions and forwarding among all admitted peers. It defaults to false. Provider introductions include exact member/incarnation metadata; the RTC client can require it and expose it for logical roster binding. The P2P admission provider authenticates a fixed match without creating a gameplay authority lease. Its current creator transport and credential-issuance boundaries remain explicit.
